items.title: 14.3.3 Derivation of Useful Results of Cross Products (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Is sabaq mein hum definition ko sab se aasan vectors par lagayenge: unit vectors \(\underline{i}, \underline{j}, \underline{k}\). Yeh nataij (results) aage har sawal mein kaam aayenge, khaas taur par 14.3.5 ke determinant formula mein. Is liye inhein achhi tarah samajh lijiye, ratta nahin.
Cross product ki definition ko unit vectors \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\) aur \(\underline{k}\) par lagane se yeh milta hai:

blocks.alt: Three axes from the origin O: z upwards, y to the right and x slanting down to the left. Short thick arrows i, j and k of length one lie along the x-, y- and z-axes.
blocks.caption: Figure: unit vectors i, j, k along the axes (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text:
(a) Har unit vector ka apne aap se cross product:
\[\underline{i} \times \underline{i} = |\underline{i}||\underline{i}|\sin 0^{\circ}\,\underline{n} = \underline{0}\]
\[\underline{j} \times \underline{j} = |\underline{j}||\underline{j}|\sin 0^{\circ}\,\underline{n} = \underline{0}\]
\[\underline{k} \times \underline{k} = |\underline{k}||\underline{k}|\sin 0^{\circ}\,\underline{n} = \underline{0}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kyun: kisi vector aur khud us ke darmiyan angle \(0^{\circ}\) hota hai, aur \(\sin 0^{\circ} = 0\). Pichle sabaq (14.3.2) mein dekha tha ke parallel vectors ka cross product zero vector hota hai, aur har vector apne aap ke parallel hai. Dhyan dein: dot product mein \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i} = 1\) tha, magar cross product mein \(\underline{i} \times \underline{i} = \underline{0}\). Dono ko mila mat dijiye.

(b) Do mukhtalif unit vectors ka cross product:
\[\underline{i} \times \underline{j} = |\underline{i}||\underline{j}|\sin 90^{\circ}\,\underline{k} = \underline{k}\]
\[\underline{j} \times \underline{k} = |\underline{j}||\underline{k}|\sin 90^{\circ}\,\underline{i} = \underline{i}\]
\[\underline{k} \times \underline{i} = |\underline{k}||\underline{i}|\sin 90^{\circ}\,\underline{j} = \underline{j}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kyun: \(\underline{i}, \underline{j}, \underline{k}\) aapas mein perpendicular hain, to \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\) aur \(\sin 90^{\circ} = 1\). Har ek ki lambai 1 hai, is liye har product ki lambai \(1 \cdot 1 \cdot 1 = 1\).
Ab direction: right hand ki ungliyan \(\underline{i}\) (yani \(x\)-axis) ki taraf rakhiye aur \(\underline{j}\) (\(y\)-axis) ki taraf modiye. Angootha \(z\)-axis ki taraf upar jata hai, is liye \(\underline{n} = \underline{k}\). Isi tarah \(\underline{j} \times \underline{k}\) mein \(\underline{n} = \underline{i}\) aur \(\underline{k} \times \underline{i}\) mein \(\underline{n} = \underline{j}\). Figure dekh kar haath se khud try kijiye.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Kitab ki line mein \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\) istemal hua hai. Idea yeh hai ke \(\underline{v}\) se wapas \(\underline{u}\) ki taraf ghoomna ulti simt (direction) mein \(\theta\) ka ghoomna hai.
Isay samajhne ka aasan tareeqa: \(\underline{v} \times \underline{u}\) ki lambai wahi \(|\underline{v}||\underline{u}|\sin\theta\) hai (numbers ki zarb mein tarteeb se farq nahin parta), lekin right hand rule mein ab ungliyan \(\underline{v}\) se \(\underline{u}\) ki taraf mudti hain, to angootha ulta ho jata hai: direction \(-\underline{n}\). Is liye \(\underline{v} \times \underline{u} = -(\underline{u} \times \underline{v})\).
Matlab cross product commutative (tarteeb se be-parwah) nahin hai; tarteeb badlo to sign badal jata hai. Is se yeh bhi mil gaya:
\[\underline{j} \times \underline{i} = -\underline{k},\quad \underline{k} \times \underline{j} = -\underline{i}\]
\[\underline{i} \times \underline{k} = -\underline{j}\]

(d) Kisi bhi vector ka apne aap se cross product:
\[\underline{u} \times \underline{u} = |\underline{u}||\underline{u}|\sin 0\,\underline{n} = \underline{0}\]

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Kitab ka note: \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\) aur \(\underline{k}\) ke cross products ek cyclic (chakkar wale) pattern mein likhe jate hain. Di gayi figure is pattern ko yaad rakhne mein madad karti hai.

blocks.alt: A circle with i at the lower left, j at the lower right and k at the top. Arrows around the circle go from i to j, from j to k and from k back to i.
blocks.caption: Figure: the cyclic pattern i → j → k → i (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Circle ko aise parhiye: teer (arrows) ki simt mein chalein (\(\underline{i} \to \underline{j} \to \underline{k} \to \underline{i}\)), to do saath wale vectors ka product teesra vector hai, plus sign ke saath: \(\underline{i} \times \underline{j} = \underline{k}\), \(\underline{j} \times \underline{k} = \underline{i}\), \(\underline{k} \times \underline{i} = \underline{j}\).
Teer ke ulat chalein to minus aata hai: \(\underline{j} \times \underline{i} = -\underline{k}\), \(\underline{k} \times \underline{j} = -\underline{i}\), \(\underline{i} \times \underline{k} = -\underline{j}\).
Yaad rakhne ka chhota tareeqa: alphabet ki tarteeb i, j, k, i, j... mein aage chalna plus, peeche chalna minus. Neeche wala table bhi isi ka khulasa hai.

blocks.caption: Row vector × column vector, e.g. row j, column k gives j × k = i (our summary table)

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Hamari misaal, kitab ka sawal nahin.) \((\underline{i} + \underline{j}) \times (\underline{i} - \underline{j})\) nikaliye. Distributive property (14.3.4 (iii)) se char hisse banenge:
\(\underline{i} \times \underline{i} = \underline{0}\), \(\underline{i} \times (-\underline{j}) = -\underline{k}\), \(\underline{j} \times \underline{i} = -\underline{k}\), \(\underline{j} \times (-\underline{j}) = \underline{0}\).
Jama: \(\underline{0} - \underline{k} - \underline{k} + \underline{0} = -2\underline{k}\).
Kyun: table se har chhota product dekha aur sign ka khayal rakha. Jawab \(-2\underline{k}\) dono vectors (jo \(xy\)-plane mein hain) par perpendicular hai, jaisa hona chahiye.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(\underline{k} \times \underline{i}\) aur \(\underline{i} \times \underline{k}\) mein se kaun sa \(\underline{j}\) hai? (Jawab: \(\underline{k} \times \underline{i} = \underline{j}\), kyun ke \(k \to i\) teer ki simt mein hai; \(\underline{i} \times \underline{k} = -\underline{j}\).)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\underline{i} \times \underline{i} = \underline{j} \times \underline{j} = \underline{k} \times \underline{k} = \underline{0}\).
2. \(\underline{i} \times \underline{j} = \underline{k}\), \(\underline{j} \times \underline{k} = \underline{i}\), \(\underline{k} \times \underline{i} = \underline{j}\) (cyclic tarteeb).
3. Ulti tarteeb par minus: \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = -\underline{v} \times \underline{u}\).
4. Har vector ke liye \(\underline{u} \times \underline{u} = \underline{0}\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\underline{i} \times \underline{k} = \underline{j}\) likh dena: \(i\) se \(k\) teer ke ulat hai, is liye \(\underline{i} \times \underline{k} = -\underline{j}\).
2. \(\underline{i} \times \underline{i} = 1\) likhna: yeh dot product \(\underline{i} \cdot \underline{i}\) ka jawab hai. Cross product mein \(\underline{i} \times \underline{i} = \underline{0}\).
3. \(\underline{u} \times \underline{v} = \underline{v} \times \underline{u}\) samajhna: tarteeb badlo to sign badal jata hai. Har sawal mein pehle dekh lijiye ke kaun sa vector pehle hai.
